chunks: And fear a Day when no soul will suffice for another in the least, nor will intercession be accepted from it, nor will ransom be taken from it, nor will they be helped.

key_terms.يَوْمًا: A day (specifically the Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What happens to intercession and ransom on the Day of Judgment according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the ultimate sovereignty of God by negating all forms of mediation—whether intercession (shafa'ah), compensation (adl), or aid—except by His leave. It highlights the individual accountability of the soul, reinforcing the concept that while the Ahl al-Bayt may intercede, their authority is derived solely from divine permission, not independent power. This serves as a profound reminder of the Day of Judgment's gravity, where worldly connections hold no sway.
